study: Babinski et al. 2018 (DCCS teacher PD for ELs, Duke, AERJ 55(1))
eval_evidence: The authors (Babinski et al., Duke University) developed the DCCS program ('we developed a list of...') and conducted the RCT under IES grant R305A120290 to Duke -- developer-conducted.
developer_evidence: 'On-site instructional coaching was available approximately every six weeks from a member of the research team'; the research team delivered the PD modules and coaching.
cascade_evidence: Research-team members delivered the workshops and on-site coaching directly to teachers; no intermediary trainer tier.
counterfactual_evidence: Comparison was a waitlist / business-as-usual control (matched school pairs, control got usual practice).
coaching_evidence: On-site instructional coaching available approximately every six weeks from the research team, plus 30-min weekly ESL/classroom-teacher collaboration; the every-6-week on-site coaching falls just below the monthly+ anchor for frequent_inclass.
student_dose_evidence: Teacher PD program (workshops, coaching, teacher-teacher collaboration); only the teachers' instruction changes. No student-facing tutoring/pull-out dose.
maturity_evidence: DCCS is delivered across a single school year (modules, coaching, collaboration throughout the school year) with end-of-year student assessment; one-year program, teachers new to it, no maturity axis.
